> 1,000 paying users on a 60/25/10/4/1 mix: about ৳126,000/month gross; infrastructure ৳3,700–9,300; net roughly ৳117,000–123,000 before tax and your time.

Lets consider the worst case scenario. What if I get 500 paying users only on Starter plan, will I survive.

> Your time is the constraint: manual monthly verification and support. Annual plans and self-service are what make 1,000+ users workable.

I'll be using SSLCOMMERZ for payment gateway instead of manual payments after the the business gain some momentum.

Note: Propose a way to show the 3m/6m/1year plan prices on the same card for better exposure.

{"kind":"reasoning","id":"p1-c7bea1b1","text":"The user asks:
1. Worst case: 500 paying users, all on Starter. Will I survive? Need compute revenue, Supabase cost, support/verification time, SSLCommerz fees.
2. SSLCommerz after momentum: need current SSLCommerz pricing/fees (research). Also settlement time, setup cost, requirements (business registration?).
3. Propose a way to show 3m/6m/1y prices on the same card for better exposure. Need inspect current paywall card UI to propose a design (plan rows? chips? segmented control? expansion?). We're in plan mode, read-only.

Let me compute the worst case:

500 Starter users. Which price? Monthly 60, 3m 180, 6m 300, 12m 600. If all monthly: 500 × 60 = ৳30,000/month gross. Supabase $25 ≈ ৳3,090 (Micro). If compute Small $15 → $15? Wait, $25 includes $10 credit; Small $15 → net $30. So infra $25–30. Gross margin ~90%. Net ~৳26,000–26,900 before tax/time.

But 500 Starter users all monthly: manual verification 500 × 2 min = 1,000 min = 16.7 hours/month. Plus support. At ৳500/hr, verification time costs ৳8,333/month. Support: if 5% need 10 min/month = 25 users × 10 min = 250 min = 4.2 hours = ৳2,083. Total time cost ~৳10,400. Net after time ~৳15,600/month (~$126). That's a side income, not a living, but "survive" yes.

But if all 500 are annual: 500 × 600 = ৳300,000/year = ৳25,000/month equivalent. Slightly less than monthly (because annual is discounted). Same infra. Net ~৳22,000/month before time, but admin is 1/12: 500/12 ≈ 42 renewals/month × 2 min = 84 min = ৳700. Support same. Net after time ~৳19,000/month. So annual is better operationally but slightly lower revenue.

If all 500 on 3-month: 500 × 180 = ৳90,000 per quarter = ৳30,000/month equivalent; verification 500/3 ≈ 167/month × 2 min = 5.6 hr = ৳2,800. Net ~৳24,000.

So worst case 500 Starter: revenue ৳25,000–30,000/month, infra ~৳3,100–3,700, time ~৳5,000–10,000. Net ৳15,000–25,000/month. In Bangladesh, that's a modest income — maybe enough to survive if solo and low costs, but not a strong business. Also, 500 paying users is actually a success; the "worst case" is all on the cheapest plan.

Need to consider SSLCommerz fees. Research current SSLCommerz pricing: I recall SSLCommerz charges 2.5% for domestic cards, 3.5% for international, 1.5% for mobile banking? Let me research. Also setup/annual fees? SSLCommerz may have a one-time setup fee (BDT 10,000?) and annual fee (BDT 5,000?), or free? Need current info. Let me spawn researcher-web with a focused question: SSLCommerz pricing (setup, annual, per-transaction for cards/bKash/Nagad/Rocket), settlement, requirements.

Also, payment gateway fees change the math: 2.5% of ৳30,000 = ৳750/month; not huge. If 3.5%, ৳1,050. Fine.

But there may be a minimum monthly fee or annual fee. Research.

Also, taxes: SSLCommerz may deduct VAT? The gateway fee may include VAT. Need to check.

3. Showing 3m/6m/1y on the same card: The current UI is `_TierCard` with the tier name, note, case ceiling, and plan rows. Need to inspect the rest of `_TierCard` (lines 480-547) to see how plans are rendered (radio? buttons?). We read 250-479; the plan rows are after 480. Let me read 480-547. Also check the paywall layout above (header, sections) to propose a design.

Proposal ideas:
- **Three price chips in one row** under the tier name: "3 mo ৳180 | 6 mo ৳300 | 1 yr ৳600", with the annual highlighted "Save ৳120" (or "2 months free"). Tapping a chip selects that term; a single "Choose Starter" button at the bottom. This shows all prices at once without expanding the card.
- **Segmented control** (3/6/12) above a single price + CTA. Good on mobile, but only shows one price at a time.
- **Price grid** 3 columns × 1 row, each column a tappable tile with term, price, and per-month equivalent; annual tile gets a "Best Value" badge. Then one CTA. This is the best exposure: all prices visible, comparison easy, one tap to select.
- **Horizontal scroll chips** if width is tight; but 3 chips fit on a phone.

The user asks "Propose a way to show the 3m/6m/1year plan prices on the same card for better exposure." So propose a layout. We should also consider the 1-month option for Starter/Pro; the card would have 4 terms. Maybe show 1m/3m/6m/12m as four tiles? On a narrow phone, 4 tiles at ~80px each = 320px, feasible. Or show 1m as a small "or ৳60 monthly" text, and 3/6/12 as the main tiles. The user specifically wants 3/6/12 exposure; the 1-month can be a secondary line.

Design proposal:
- Tier card header: name + note + case ceiling.
- A 3-column row of term tiles: 3 Months / 6 Months / 1 Year, each with the absolute price and the effective monthly (৳60/month). The annual tile has a "2 Months Free" badge; the 6-month "1 Month Free".
- Below: a single primary CTA "Choose Starter" that uses the selected tile; default selection = 1 Year (best value) or 6 Months.
- A small "Prefer monthly? ৳60/month" text link for Starter/Pro, so the 1-month option isn't lost.
- For Firm/Firm Plus/Enterprise, the same three tiles (no monthly link).
- Visual hierarchy: annual tile filled with primary container, others outlined; selected state with a check.
- Accessibility: each tile has a semantic label ("3 months, 180 taka, 60 taka per month"); min 48px tap targets.
- Bengali: numbers localized, "মাস" / "বছর"; currency "৳" prefix; ensure no overflow at large font sizes; use `Wrap` or `LayoutBuilder` to stack 2+1 on very narrow screens.

This is a UI proposal; no code. Need to check the current card's plan rows to see if this replaces them. Let me read the rest of paywall_screen.dart.

Also, the current paywall `_TierCard` likely renders each plan as a row/button. Replacing with a grid is a change. The user asks to propose, so describe.

Could also propose a **comparison table** across tiers with columns 3/6/12, but on mobile that's wide. Better per-card tiles.

Another idea: **"Starting at ৳50/month"** on the card, with term chips. But the user wants absolute prices visible.

Let me read the rest of the card and the checkout to understand the plan selection flow. Then propose.

Also, the user asks "will I survive" — need to define "survive." As a solo founder in Bangladesh, ৳15k–25k/month net is below a typical lawyer's income but maybe enough to keep the app alive as a side project. The honest answer: yes, the app survives financially (infra is covered), but it won't pay a full-time salary; you'd need ~1,000+ Starter users or a better mix. Also, 500 Starter users at ৳60 is ৳30k/month gross, which is roughly a junior developer's salary in Dhaka? Not sure; avoid specific salary comparisons unless verified. Could say "a modest side income, not a full-time living" in plain terms.

Let me compute exact scenarios:

**500 Starter, all monthly:**
- Gross: 500 × 60 = ৳30,000/mo.
- Supabase: $25 = ৳3,090; with Small compute $30 = ৳3,707. Say ৳3,100–3,700.
- SSLCommerz fee: assume 2.5% = ৳750 (if domestic cards); bKash 1.5%? Need research. Let's wait.
- Verification: 500 × 2 min = 16.7 hr; at ৳500/hr = ৳8,333. With SSLCommerz, automatic — no manual verification. That's a key benefit: gateway removes the ৳8,333 time cost but adds ~2.5% fee (৳750). Great trade.
- Support: 5% × 10 min = 4.2 hr = ৳2,083.
- Net cash: 30,000 − 3,700 − 750 = ৳25,550 before tax and support time.
- After support time (৳2,083): ৳23,467.
- After tax? Unknown. If 15% VAT, ৳4,500, net ~৳19,000. But don't assert VAT; mention as a caveat.

**500 Starter, all annual:**
- Gross: 500 × 600 = ৳300,000/year = ৳25,000/mo.
- Supabase same.
- Gateway fee 2.5% = ৳625/mo equivalent.
- Support same.
- Net cash: 25,000 − 3,700 − 625 = ৳20,675; after support ~৳18,600.
- No manual verification.

**500 Starter, all 3-month:**
- Gross: 500 × 180 / 3 = ৳30,000/mo.
- Gateway fee 2.5% = ৳750.
- Net similar to monthly.

So monthly/3-month yield ৳30k gross; annual yields ৳25k gross. Monthly is better revenue but more transactions (gateway handles it). With a gateway, monthly is fine operationally. Without, annual is better.

**500 Starter, worst case with no gateway (manual):** net after time ~৳21k–23k. Still survives.

**What does "survive" mean?** If the app is a side project, yes. If it's your only income, ৳20k–25k/month net is thin. Need ~1,000 Starter users for ৳50k–60k gross, net ~৳45k–50k. Or a mix with Firm tiers. State clearly.

Also, the worst case isn't 500 Starter; it's 500 Starter **and high support**. If 20% need 10 min/month: 100 users × 10 min = 16.7 hr = ৳8,333; net ~৳17k. Still positive.

Also, churn: if 5% monthly churn, you need 25 new users/month just to stay at 500. Acquisition cost unknown. Mention.

Now, SSLCommerz research. Let me spawn researcher with a focused question:
- Current pricing: setup fee, annual fee, transaction fees for cards, bKash, Nagad, Rocket, internet banking; settlement time; requirements (trade license, TIN, bank account); sandbox; recurring payments support? The app sells subscriptions; SSLCommerz may not support recurring billing automatically. This matters: even with a gateway, subscriptions may require manual renewal or a recurring API. Does SSLCommerz support recurring? I think SSLCommerz has a "Recurring Payment" API for cards, but bKash recurring? Need research. If no recurring, the gateway only automates one-time payments; users still need to renew manually, but verification is automatic. That's still a big win.
- Also, fees may be 2.5% for domestic cards, 3.5% international, 1.5% bKash? Let's get facts.

Also, the gateway may require a business entity (trade license) and a minimum monthly volume. The user may be a solo developer; this is a practical blocker. Research.

Let me spawn two researcher agents in parallel? One for SSLCommerz pricing/fees/requirements, one for recurring support/settlement. Or one comprehensive prompt. The tool allows multiple agents. Use one detailed prompt; maybe two for independent questions: (1) pricing/fees, (2) recurring/settlement/requirements. Let me do two.

Also, read the rest of paywall card. Let me do both in parallel: read files + spawn agents.

Need to check current checkout for plan selection: `paywall_screen.dart` lines 480-547, and maybe `checkout_screen.dart`. The card's plan rows. Let me read.","open":false,"collapse":"preview"}

**SSLCOMMERZ publicly documents regular checkout payments, but I could not verify a generally available subscription or recurring-charge API in its official documentation.** In particular, the public material does **not** establish that merchants can automatically debit a saved card each billing period, or set up recurring bKash/Nagad mandates through the gateway.

| Payment type | What the official material supports | Recurring/subscription conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| **Cards** | Card payments through the regular checkout flow. SSLCOMMERZ also documents Google Pay checkout using cards saved in a customer’s Google Account, and a `user_refer` value associated with card tokenization. | **Not confirmed as recurring billing.** The public docs I found do not document a reusable card-token charge endpoint, subscription scheduler, or merchant-initiated recurring-charge workflow. Tokenization or saved-card checkout alone does not establish that the merchant can automatically charge later. |
| **bKash/Nagad** | The current pricing page lists bKash and Nagad among standard payment channels. The integration docs describe a checkout flow and list mobile-banking gateways. | **No public SSLCOMMERZ documentation found for recurring bKash/Nagad mandates or auto-debits.** Channel availability for a payment is not evidence of recurring authorization. |

The standard [SSLCOMMERZ integration documentation](https://developer.sslcommerz.com/doc/v4/) describes creating a transaction session, receiving a payment notification (IPN), and validating the order. That is a transaction-checkout flow, not a published subscription API. The [Google Pay integration guide](https://developer.sslcommerz.com/doc/v4/google-pay-integration.html) describes saved Google Pay cards and `user_refer`-based tokenization, but does not document subsequent merchant-initiated recurring charges. The [pricing page](https://sslcommerz.com/pricing/) lists bKash and Nagad as payment channels, but does not describe recurring mandates.

**Practical answer:** Treat automatic recurring billing—on cards or bKash/Nagad—as **unconfirmed from public official documentation**, not as a standard feature you can rely on. Before designing around it, ask SSLCOMMERZ to confirm in writing whether your merchant account can access a recurring/card-on-file product, its API specification, and any channel-specific approval requirements. The public docs do not set out a recurring-specific approval process.

## Merchant account: documents and onboarding

The official [Onboarding Requirements](https://sslcommerz.com/onboarding-requirements/) page gives requirements by business type. Common items include a current trade licence, TIN, business bank details and cheque leaf, signatory identification and photo, and a completed Merchant Enrollment Form (MEF). Requirements vary by entity and sector.

- **Proprietorship:** updated trade licence; company bank account and bank cheque leaf; signatory’s NID and attested passport-size photo; TIN certificate; completed, signed and sealed MEF; DBID. Additional items may apply—for example, a drug licence for a pharmacy or an ISP licence/declaration where necessary.
- **Private/public limited company:** updated trade licence; incorporation certificate; MOA/AOA; Form XII; company bank cheque leaf; company BIN/VAT certificate; TIN certificate; and relevant owner/signatory/shareholder NID and photo; completed, signed and sealed MEF.
- **Partnership:** trade licence; partnership deed; company BIN; TIN certificate; signatory’s NID and photo; authorization letter for the signatory; company bank cheque leaf; DBID; completed, signed and sealed MEF.
- **Sector-dependent extras:** the onboarding checklist names other permissions or licences for some businesses—such as import/export, pharmacy, travel/Hajj, ISP, education and medical services. The checklist also refers to address verification and consistency of the merchant name across documents.

The precise checklist depends on the merchant’s legal form and business. Use the linked official page as the working list and confirm with SSLCOMMERZ which items apply to your case.

### Website or app review

SSLCOMMERZ’s published [website terms and conditions](https://sslcommerz.com/terms-and-conditions/) list website review requirements, including:

- Terms and Conditions, Return/Refund Policy and Privacy Policy in the footer.
- About Us/company and management details, registered address, and trade-licence or TIN number on the site.
- A live site—not a demo or maintenance site—plus product stock information and the payment banner.
- A stated refund timeline and delivery information.
- A checkout checkbox requiring customers to agree to the linked terms and policies.

The published checklist is framed around a **website**. I did not find a comparable public app-review checklist, so app-only businesses should ask SSLCOMMERZ what app screens, URLs or other evidence it needs for review.

The [merchant terms](https://signup.sslcommerz.com/term-condition) say the merchant receives test and live APIs, and that service goes live after technical feasibility and a proper integration handshake. They also say the merchant is expected to sign a formal agreement within one month of going live.

## Approval time

I found **no SSLCOMMERZ-published approval-time SLA**. Its homepage describes online onboarding and quick activation, but does not promise a number of days. An SSLCOMMERZ article about merchant-account setup says approval can range from **a few days to a few weeks**; it presents this as a general range, not a guaranteed SSLCOMMERZ processing time. - **Six tiers, seventeen plans:** Free (৳0, 50 cases), Starter (৳60/month, 500 cases, 1 device), Pro (৳120/month, 1,000 cases, 2 devices), Firm (৳250/month, 2,500 cases, 5 members), Firm Plus (৳500/month, 6,000 cases, 12 members) and Enterprise (৳1,500/month, unlimited, fair use).

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.cancel_subscription()
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'pg_catalog', 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  -- The account is the session's own, never a parameter: this ends the caller's
  -- plan or nothing.
  v_user_id uuid := auth.uid();
  v_profile public.profiles%rowtype;
  v_plan_type text;
  v_amount integer;
  v_now timestamptz := now();
  v_previous_expiry timestamptz;
  v_cancelled_at timestamptz;
begin
  if v_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  select * into v_profile
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = v_user_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  -- A member's plan is the chamber's (§5.1), so their own row is not where their
  -- entitlement lives and ending it would change nothing while silently
  -- discarding paid time they keep for later. Refused instead. The owner is not
  -- a member: his own row *is* the chamber's plan, and the existing
  -- `mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm()` carries the new expiry to it.
  if v_profile.firm_id is not null
     and v_profile.role in ('associate', 'viewer') then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'firm_member');
  end if;

  -- Only a live paid period can be cancelled, and the test is the same derived
  -- rule every gate reads, so this cannot disagree with `is_premium()` about
  -- whether anything is running.
  if v_profile.subscription_expiry is null
     or v_profile.subscription_expiry + interval '48 hours' <= v_now then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'no_active_plan');
  end if;

  v_previous_expiry := v_profile.subscription_expiry;

  -- The plan that is running is the newest approved purchase — the same rule the
  -- app's Current Plan uses — and the amount recorded is what was actually paid
  -- for it rather than today's price list.
  select s.plan_type, s.amount
    into v_plan_type, v_amount
    from public.payment_submissions s
   where s.user_id = v_user_id
     and s.status = 'approved'
   order by coalesce(s.approved_at, s.submitted_at) desc
   limit 1;

  -- Backdated past the 48-hour grace, with an hour of cushion at the boundary,
  -- so the next entitlement check is false rather than true for two more days.
  -- The stored tier is deliberately untouched: it is the record of the last tier
  -- held, and it is what gives the account its lapse allowance (Pro 100,
  -- Firm 500, Firm Plus 1,000) instead of dropping it to Free.
  update public.profiles p
     set subscription_expiry = v_now - interval '49 hours',
         subscription_status = 'cancelled'
   where p.id = v_user_id;

  insert into public.subscription_cancellations (
    user_id, plan_type, amount, previous_expiry, cancelled_at
  )
  values (v_user_id, v_plan_type, v_amount, v_previous_expiry, v_now)
  returning cancelled_at into v_cancelled_at;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'cancelled',
    'plan_type', v_plan_type,
    'amount', v_amount,
    'previous_expiry', v_previous_expiry,
    'cancelled_at', v_cancelled_at
  );
end;
$function$

-- project on 2026-10-19.
--
-- **Why this file exists, and why it is a reconstruction.** The cancellation
-- table, its own-row policy and `cancel_subscription()` were applied to the
-- writable project `lsthasywrdrhuuxnykau` on 2026-10-18 under version
-- `20261018100000`, but that version was recorded **without its statements**
-- and no migration file was committed. The app therefore called an RPC that no
-- file in this repository defined, and `tool/apply_supabase_migrations.dart`
-- reported the version as drift. This file is that missing record: the table,
-- policy, grants and function are copied from the applied project's own
-- catalogs (`pg_get_functiondef`, `information_schema`, `pg_policies`,
-- `pg_class`) rather than invented from the client's call sites.
--
-- The version in the filename is the version the live project already holds, so
-- the applier skips it there and its history stays truthful. Every statement is
-- idempotent (`if not exists`, `create or replace`, `drop policy if exists`), so
-- a fresh project can apply this file and re-running it changes nothing.
--
-- Table class: `subscription_cancellations` is **server-managed**. Only
-- `cancel_subscription()` writes it, and a signed-in client may select its own
-- rows under RLS; there is deliberately no insert, update or delete policy.
--
-- Proven on 2026-10-19 by running this file inside a rolled-back transaction on
-- the applied project (it re-created the same objects with no error) and by the
-- client's own cancellation cases in
-- `test/features/subscription_details_screen_test.dart`.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. The ledger row.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create table if not exists public.subscription_cancellations (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  -- The plan that was running and what was actually paid for it. Both are
  -- nullable because a period granted outside the ladder has no purchase row to
  -- name; the cancellation still happened and its expiry is still a fact.
  plan_type text,
  amount integer,
  -- The expiry that was ended, and the instant it was ended. Both required:
  -- a cancellation without either cannot be reconciled against a statement.
  previous_expiry timestamptz not null,
  cancelled_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

comment on table public.subscription_cancellations is
  'Server-managed. One row per cancelled paid plan: the plan that was running, what was paid for it, the expiry that was ended and the instant it was cancelled. Written only by cancel_subscription(); the client may read its own rows.';

-- One account's ledger, newest first — the read the Subscription History list
-- makes.
create index if not exists subscription_cancellations_user_cancelled_at_idx
  on public.subscription_cancellations (user_id, cancelled_at desc);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Read your own rows, and nothing else.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table public.subscription_cancellations enable row level security;

-- RLS is a second fence, not the first: the table-level grants are narrowed to
-- the one verb a client needs, so even a mistake in a policy cannot let a
-- client write this ledger.
revoke all on table public.subscription_cancellations from public, anon, authenticated;
grant select on table public.subscription_cancellations to authenticated;
grant all on table public.subscription_cancellations to service_role;

drop policy if exists subscription_cancellations_select_own
  on public.subscription_cancellations;
create policy subscription_cancellations_select_own
  on public.subscription_cancellations
  for select
  using (user_id = auth.uid());

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. The one write path.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.cancel_subscription()
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  -- The account is the session's own, never a parameter: this ends the caller's
  -- plan or nothing.
  v_user_id uuid := auth.uid();
  v_profile public.profiles%rowtype;
  v_plan_type text;
  v_amount integer;
  v_now timestamptz := now();
  v_previous_expiry timestamptz;
  v_cancelled_at timestamptz;
begin
  if v_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
  end if;

  select * into v_profile
    from public.profiles p
   where p.id = v_user_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  -- A member's plan is the chamber's (§5.1), so their own row is not where their
  -- entitlement lives and ending it would change nothing while silently
  -- discarding paid time they keep for later. Refused instead. The owner is not
  -- a member: his own row *is* the chamber's plan, and the existing
  -- `mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm()` carries the new expiry to it.
  if v_profile.firm_id is not null
     and v_profile.role in ('associate', 'viewer') then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'firm_member');
  end if;

  -- Only a live paid period can be cancelled, and the test is the same derived
  -- rule every gate reads, so this cannot disagree with `is_premium()` about
  -- whether anything is running.
  if v_profile.subscription_expiry is null
     or v_profile.subscription_expiry + interval '48 hours' <= v_now then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'no_active_plan');
  end if;

  v_previous_expiry := v_profile.subscription_expiry;

  -- The plan that is running is the newest approved purchase — the same rule the
  -- app's Current Plan uses — and the amount recorded is what was actually paid
  -- for it rather than today's price list.
  select s.plan_type, s.amount
    into v_plan_type, v_amount
    from public.payment_submissions s
   where s.user_id = v_user_id
     and s.status = 'approved'
   order by coalesce(s.approved_at, s.submitted_at) desc
   limit 1;

  -- Backdated past the 48-hour grace, with an hour of cushion at the boundary,
  -- so the next entitlement check is false rather than true for two more days.
  -- The stored tier is deliberately untouched: it is the record of the last tier
  -- held, and it is what gives the account its lapse allowance (Starter 100,
  -- Pro 250, Firm 500, Firm Plus 1,000, Enterprise 2,000) instead of dropping it
  -- to Free.
  update public.profiles p
     set subscription_expiry = v_now - interval '49 hours',
         subscription_status = 'cancelled'
   where p.id = v_user_id;

  insert into public.subscription_cancellations (
    user_id, plan_type, amount, previous_expiry, cancelled_at
  )
  values (v_user_id, v_plan_type, v_amount, v_previous_expiry, v_now)
  returning cancelled_at into v_cancelled_at;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'cancelled',
    'plan_type', v_plan_type,
    'amount', v_amount,
    'previous_expiry', v_previous_expiry,
    'cancelled_at', v_cancelled_at
  );
end;
$$;

comment on function public.cancel_subscription() is
  'Ends the caller''s own live paid plan: backdates subscription_expiry past the 48-hour grace so entitlement is false at once, records one subscription_cancellations row (plan, amount, the expiry ended, the instant) and leaves the stored tier alone so the account lands on its lapse allowance. Answers status firm_member for an associate or viewer (the chamber holds the plan), no_active_plan for a free or lapsed account, not_found without a profile row, and unauthenticated without a session.';

-- The RPC is for signed-in callers only. `create or replace` preserves an ACL,
-- but stating it here is what makes this file a complete record: a fresh project
-- gets the same answer as the live one.
revoke all on function public.cancel_subscription() from public, anon;
grant execute on function public.cancel_subscription() to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.cancel_subscription() to service_role;
"}}

+-- Subscription History — cancelling a live plan, reconstructed from the live
+-- project on 2026-10-19.
+--
+-- **Why this file exists, and why it is a reconstruction.** The cancellation
+-- table, its own-row policy and `cancel_subscription()` were applied to the
+-- writable project `lsthasywrdrhuuxnykau` on 2026-10-18 under version
+-- `20261018100000`, but that version was recorded **without its statements**
+-- and no migration file was committed. The app therefore called an RPC that no
+-- file in this repository defined, and `tool/apply_supabase_migrations.dart`
+-- reported the version as drift. This file is that missing record: the table,
+-- policy, grants and function are copied from the applied project's own
+-- catalogs (`pg_get_functiondef`, `information_schema`, `pg_policies`,
+-- `pg_class`) rather than invented from the client's call sites. The function's
+-- logic is byte-for-byte the live one; only its lapse-allowance comment was
+-- updated from the old Pro/Firm/Firm Plus numbers to the six-tier ladder's.
+--
+-- The version in the filename is the version the live project already holds, so
+-- the applier skips it there and its history stays truthful. Every statement is
+-- idempotent (`if not exists`, `create or replace`, `drop policy if exists`), so
+-- a fresh project can apply this file and re-running it changes nothing.
+--
+-- Table class: `subscription_cancellations` is **server-managed**. Only
+-- `cancel_subscription()` writes it, and a signed-in client may select its own
+-- rows under RLS; there is deliberately no insert, update or delete policy.
+--
+-- Proven on 2026-10-19 by running this file inside a rolled-back transaction on
+-- the applied project (it re-created the same objects with no error) and by the
+-- client's own cancellation cases in
+-- `test/features/subscription_details_screen_test.dart`.
+
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- 1. The ledger row.
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+create table if not exists public.subscription_cancellations (
+  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
+  user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
+  -- The plan that was running and what was actually paid for it. Both are
+  -- nullable because a period granted outside the ladder has no purchase row to
+  -- name; the cancellation still happened and its expiry is still a fact.
+  plan_type text,
+  amount integer,
+  -- The expiry that was ended, and the instant it was ended. Both required:
+  -- a cancellation without either cannot be reconciled against a statement.
+  previous_expiry timestamptz not null,
+  cancelled_at timestamptz not null default now()
+);
+
+comment on table public.subscription_cancellations is
+  'Server-managed. One row per cancelled paid plan: the plan that was running, what was paid for it, the expiry that was ended and the instant it was cancelled. Written only by cancel_subscription(); the client may read its own rows.';
+
+-- One account's ledger, newest first — the read the Subscription History list
+-- makes.
+create index if not exists subscription_cancellations_user_cancelled_at_idx
+  on public.subscription_cancellations (user_id, cancelled_at desc);
+
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- 2. Read your own rows, and nothing else.
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+alter table public.subscription_cancellations enable row level security;
+
+-- RLS is a second fence, not the first: the table-level grants are narrowed to
+-- the one verb a client needs, so even a mistake in a policy cannot let a
+-- client write this ledger.
+revoke all on table public.subscription_cancellations from public, anon, authenticated;
+grant select on table public.subscription_cancellations to authenticated;
+grant all on table public.subscription_cancellations to service_role;
+
+drop policy if exists subscription_cancellations_select_own
+  on public.subscription_cancellations;
+create policy subscription_cancellations_select_own
+  on public.subscription_cancellations
+  for select
+  using (user_id = auth.uid());
+
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- 3. The one write path.
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+create or replace function public.cancel_subscription()
+returns jsonb
+language plpgsql
+security definer
+set search_path = pg_catalog, public
+as $$
+declare
+  -- The account is the session's own, never a parameter: this ends the caller's
+  -- plan or nothing.
+  v_user_id uuid := auth.uid();
+  v_profile public.profiles%rowtype;
+  v_plan_type text;
+  v_amount integer;
+  v_now timestamptz := now();
+  v_previous_expiry timestamptz;
+  v_cancelled_at timestamptz;
+begin
+  if v_user_id is null then
+    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'unauthenticated');
+  end if;
+
+  select * into v_profile
+    from public.profiles p
+   where p.id = v_user_id
+   for update;
+
+  if not found then
+    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
+  end if;
+
+  -- A member's plan is the chamber's (§5.1), so their own row is not where their
+  -- entitlement lives and ending it would change nothing while silently
+  -- discarding paid time they keep for later. Refused instead. The owner is not
+  -- a member: his own row *is* the chamber's plan, and the existing
+  -- `mirror_owner_subscription_to_firm()` carries the new expiry to it.
+  if v_profile.firm_id is not null
+     and v_profile.role in ('associate', 'viewer') then
+    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'firm_member');
+  end if;
+
+  -- Only a live paid period can be cancelled, and the test is the same derived
+  -- rule every gate reads, so this cannot disagree with `is_premium()` about
+  -- whether anything is running.
+  if v_profile.subscription_expiry is null
+     or v_profile.subscription_expiry + interval '48 hours' <= v_now then
+    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'no_active_plan');
+  end if;
+
+  v_previous_expiry := v_profile.subscription_expiry;
+
+  -- The plan that is running is the newest approved purchase — the same rule the
+  -- app's Current Plan uses — and the amount recorded is what was actually paid
+  -- for it rather than today's price list.
+  select s.plan_type, s.amount
+    into v_plan_type, v_amount
+    from public.payment_submissions s
+   where s.user_id = v_user_id
+     and s.status = 'approved'
+   order by coalesce(s.approved_at, s.submitted_at) desc
+   limit 1;
+
+  -- Backdated past the 48-hour grace, with an hour of cushion at the boundary,
+  -- so the next entitlement check is false rather than true for two more days.
+  -- The stored tier is deliberately untouched: it is the record of the last tier
+  -- held, and it is what gives the account its lapse allowance (Starter 100,
+  -- Pro 250, Firm 500, Firm Plus 1,000, Enterprise 2,000) instead of dropping it
+  -- to Free.
+  update public.profiles p
+     set subscription_expiry = v_now - interval '49 hours',
+         subscription_status = 'cancelled'
+   where p.id = v_user_id;
+
+  insert into public.subscription_cancellations (
+    user_id, plan_type, amount, previous_expiry, cancelled_at
+  )
+  values (v_user_id, v_plan_type, v_amount, v_previous_expiry, v_now)
+  returning cancelled_at into v_cancelled_at;
+
+  return jsonb_build_object(
+    'status', 'cancelled',
+    'plan_type', v_plan_type,
+    'amount', v_amount,
+    'previous_expiry', v_previous_expiry,
+    'cancelled_at', v_cancelled_at
+  );
+end;
+$$;
+
+comment on function public.cancel_subscription() is
+  'Ends the caller''s own live paid plan: backdates subscription_expiry past the 48-hour grace so entitlement is false at once, records one subscription_cancellations row (plan, amount, the expiry ended, the instant) and leaves the stored tier alone so the account lands on its lapse allowance. Answers status firm_member for an associate or viewer (the chamber holds the plan), no_active_plan for a free or lapsed account, not_found without a profile row, and unauthenticated without a session.';
+
+-- The RPC is for signed-in callers only. `create or replace` preserves an ACL,
+-- but stating it here is what makes this file a complete record: a fresh project
+-- gets the same answer as the live one.
+revoke all on function public.cancel_subscription() from public, anon;
+grant execute on function public.cancel_subscription() to authenticated;
+grant execute on function public.cancel_subscription() to service_role;

It is a problem with an old **self-test script**, not with the app or your live data.

**What the script is**
`rpc_smoke_test.sql` is a manual checker for the server. You run it by hand against the live database, and it does everything inside one transaction that is rolled back at the end, so it leaves nothing behind. It needs two real accounts passed to it and uses them as stand-ins for a chamber owner and an ordinary user.

**Where it stops**
It gets most of the way through, then fails in the part that tests removing a member from a chamber. To set that scene, it tries to add a case on behalf of the test member. The server refuses with `add_not_permitted` — meaning “this account is not allowed to add records here”. The script treats that refusal as a failure and stops.

**Why that happens**
The likely reason is that the script assumes the two accounts are blank slates: no chamber of their own, no existing membership, no history. The accounts it was given are real ones with real relationships, and earlier steps in the script also move them between chambers. By the time it reaches the removal scene, the account’s membership state is not what the script expected, so the permission check correctly says no. I am labelling that as an inference: the exact state needs dedicated test accounts to confirm it.

**What it does and does not mean**
- It does **not** mean the cancellation fix, the subscription changes, or the permission rules are broken. The cancellation objects were checked directly, and the newer server checks all pass.
- It is **not** part of the app’s normal test suite, so it does not block builds or releases.
- It does mean that one old checker cannot currently be used as proof of anything, because it never reaches its final line.

**The fix**
Give it two throwaway accounts it creates itself, the way the newer ladder check does, instead of borrowing real accounts. Then its assumptions hold regardless of what is in the database. I already did that for two earlier sections of this script; the removal section is the remaining one.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.remove_firm_member(p_user_id uuid)
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'pg_catalog', 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  v_actor uuid := auth.uid();
  v_firm_id uuid;
  v_locked boolean;
begin
  if v_actor is null then
    raise exception 'unauthenticated' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  if p_user_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'invalid_request');
  end if;

  -- The caller's own firm, and only if they own it. A non-owner gets an answer
  -- rather than an error: it is a state the UI can word, not a bug.
  select f.id into v_firm_id
    from public.firms f
   where f.owner_id = v_actor;

  if v_firm_id is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_owner');
  end if;

  if p_user_id = v_actor then
    -- A firm is not transferable in this task, so removing the owner would
    -- leave `firms.owner_id` pointing at a non-member and the firm with nobody
    -- who may administer it.
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'cannot_remove_self');
  end if;

  -- Locked, so two concurrent removals cannot both claim the same row and one
  -- of them cannot report `removed` for a membership it did not delete.
  select true into v_locked
    from public.firm_members m
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id = p_user_id
   for update;

  if not found then
    return jsonb_build_object('status', 'not_found');
  end if;

  delete from public.firm_members m
   where m.firm_id = v_firm_id
     and m.user_id = p_user_id;

  -- The revocation, in one statement: `firm_id` is what every scoped read, every
  -- topic join and every queued `push_changes` write at once. `role` follows it
  -- back to the individual default rather than being left as `associate` with no
  -- firm.
  update public.profiles p
     set firm_id = null,
         role = 'individual'
   where p.id = p_user_id;

  -- The member's push registrations go with the access. A row here is keyed by
  -- the FCM token, so this reaches every device that registered one, including
  -- devices that will never sign in again to clean up after themselves.
  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = p_user_id;

  -- Two audiences, two topics — both as the trigger's own `row_change` event,
  -- so the client needs no second decoder:
  --
  --   * `user:{removed}` reaches the removed account's own devices at once,
  --     whatever topic they were joined to (`can_read_topic` always allows a
  --     caller their own user topic, including after the relink above);
  --   * `firm:{firm}` refreshes every remaining member's roster view.
  --
  -- The DELETE above fires no row trigger — the broadcast trigger is
  -- INSERT/UPDATE only — so this announcement is explicit rather than implied.
  perform realtime.send(
    jsonb_build_object('table', 'firm_members', 'id', p_user_id),
    'row_change',
    'user:' || p_user_id::text,
    true
  );
  perform realtime.send(
    jsonb_build_object('table', 'firm_members', 'id', p_user_id),
    'row_change',
    'firm:' || v_firm_id::text,
    true
  );

Progress note:
It is a problem with an old **self-test script**, not with the app or your live data.

**What the script is**
`rpc_smoke_test.sql` is a manual checker for the server. You run it by hand against the live database, and it does everything inside one transaction that is rolled back at the end, so it leaves nothing behind. It needs two real accounts passed to it and uses them as stand-ins for a chamber owner and an ordinary user.

**Where it stops**
It gets most of the way through, then fails in the part that tests removing a member from a chamber. To set that scene, it tries to add a case on behalf of the test member. The server refuses with `add_not_permitted` — meaning “this account is not allowed to add records here”. The script treats that refusal as a failure and stops.

**Why that happens**
The likely reason is that the script assumes the two accounts are blank slates: no chamber of their own, no existing membership, no history. The accounts it was given are real ones with real relationships, and earlier steps in the script also move them between chambers. By the time it reaches the removal scene, the account’s membership state is not what the script expected, so the permission check correctly says no. I am labelling that as an inference: the exact state needs dedicated test accounts to confirm it.

**What it does and does not mean**
- It does **not** mean the cancellation fix, the subscription changes, or the permission rules are broken. The cancellation objects were checked directly, and the newer server checks all pass.
- It is **not** part of the app’s normal test suite, so it does not block builds or releases.
- It does mean that one old checker cannot currently be used as proof of anything, because it never reaches its final line.

**The fix**
Give it two throwaway accounts it creates itself, the way the newer ladder check does, instead of borrowing real accounts. Then its assumptions hold regardless of what is in the database. I already did that for two earlier sections of this script; the removal section is the remaining one.

Here is what that sentence means, checked against the code rather than assumed.

**What happens when a paid plan ends**
1. On the end date, syncing still works for another **48 hours** (a grace window).
2. After that, sync stops and the account drops to its **lapse allowance** — for a Firm chamber, the **500 most recently edited cases** stay writable, and everything else becomes read-only until renewal. Nothing is deleted or hidden.

**What the app tells you today**
- A banner appears **only after the end date**: first "your subscription expired, renew to avoid losing sync", then, past the 48 hours, a red one telling the owner to renew (or an associate to ask their owner).
- The end date is printed on the Subscription Details screen — but you only see it if you open that screen.
- There is **no warning before** the date passes: no notification, no "expires in 7 days" banner, no prompt at sign-in. I checked the notification code (nothing mentions renewal or expiry) and the banner logic (it renders nothing while the plan is still active).

**Why "a monthly plan makes it more frequent"**
Firm is the only chamber tier that sells a **one-month** plan (৳300). Renewal is manual — nothing charges automatically. So a chamber on the monthly plan reaches its end date, and therefore its 500-case write ceiling, **every month** instead of once every three, six or twelve months. Each cycle is another chance to hit read-only mid-work, and each needs someone to remember to pay and have it approved.

**What a fix would look like** (not built): a pre-expiry notice — a banner from, say, seven days out plus a local reminder, addressed to the owner for a chamber, and cleared when a renewal is approved. That is a new piece of work, not a change to what exists.

{"kind":"reasoning","id":"p4-9d89a906","text":"The daily job already reads the DB and settings in an isolate and posts alerts. Adding an expiry reminder here is natural: read the local `profiles`/`firms` row for `subscription_expiry`, compare to today, and if within N days, post one notification (fixed id). This runs daily, so it would repeat each day within the window unless we make it "exactly at N days before". Better: post when `daysLeft == leadDays` (once), plus maybe again at 1 day. Simplest honest design: fire once when the plan is `leadDays` away, and once more at expiry? The post-expiry banner already covers expiry.

But this requires the app to open at least once to arm the alarm; and requires notifications enabled? `syncSchedule` arms alarms only if the default is on or cases individually enabled. So a user with hearing notifications off would get no expiry reminder from this path. That's a real constraint to state.

Alternative simpler delivery: banner only, shown whenever expiry is within N days. Always works when the app is opened, no permission, no isolate work. For a lawyer who opens the app daily (it's a diary), the banner is arguably sufficient. But "reminded" implies a notification when not in the app.

Mixed approach (best): banner from N days before (always, in-app) + a phone notification once at N days before via the existing daily job, subject to the phone's notification setting. That's a coherent, low-risk design; the banner is the guarantee, the notification is the extra.

Now, for a chamber: owner is the payer; members inherit. The owner should get both. Members should get the in-app banner too (they'll lose sync), but a "renew" notification would be wrong for them — associates get "ask your firm owner" already at expiry. For pre-expiry, keep the banner for everyone with role-appropriate wording, and the notification only for the owner/individual. That mirrors the existing post-expiry split. I can decide this without asking, following the existing pattern. But maybe ask because it's product wording.

Questions worth asking (batch, ≤4):
1. Lead time: 7 days (recommended), 3, 14.

Progress note:
Done — the app now warns a paying account **before** its plan ends, using the four answers you gave: seven days then three, banner plus one phone notification, everyone in the chamber, and no nagging beyond those two notices.

**What a lawyer will see**
- From **seven days before the end date** until the plan ends, a bar across the top of every screen: *"Your subscription ends in 7 days, on 30/10/2026. Renew to keep syncing."* On the last day it names the date only, so nothing reads "in 1 days". In a chamber every member sees it, worded as *"Your firm's plan ends in 3 days… Ask your firm owner to renew."* It cannot be dismissed, same as the existing expiry warning.
- A phone notification on the **morning of the 7-day mark and the morning of the 3-day mark** (09:00 Bangladesh time), on its own "Subscription Reminders" channel so it can be silenced separately from hearing alerts. Tapping it opens Subscription Plans.
- Nothing else changes: the red "your subscription has ended" messages still take over on the end date.

**Two safeguards worth knowing**
- The reminder re-reads the end date just before it posts, so if the chamber renewed in the meantime it stays silent instead of announcing an ending that is not happening.
- Both the bar and the notification read the same end date the app already uses to decide whether you are premium, so they can never disagree with your entitlement.

**A real bug found and fixed while checking.** My first version made the app talk to Android's alarm service on every sync even when nothing was scheduled. On the test machine that call never returned, which left the Add/Edit case sheet stuck open and broke two unrelated acceptance tests. The app now remembers which reminders it actually scheduled and, with none, touches nothing — and I added a guard test so that cannot quietly return.

**Verified:** `flutter analyze` clean · full suite **1920 tests pass** · version **0.0.555**, recorded with the script · plan, Task 21 and the session notes updated. No SQL was needed, so the Supabase ledger is untouched.

**Limitations**
- I could not watch an actual notification arrive — that needs a real phone, since the alarm service does not exist on this machine.
- The phone half only lands if that phone allows the app's notifications; the in-app bar is the part that cannot be missed.
- A plan ending *today* gets the bar but no notification, because both reminder mornings have already passed by then.

The most useful next step is a device pass on the two reminder mornings.

Done. All five items are in, and one thing needs saying clearly up front.

**The Cancel button was never removed.** It is still in the code with five tests covering it, and no version in the history touched it. It hides itself once a plan has been cancelled or has ended, which is exactly the state you were looking at — and the server would refuse a second cancellation anyway. So I did not add it back; instead the card now states plainly that the plan was cancelled, which was the missing explanation.

**What a lawyer now sees on Subscription Details**
- A cancelled plan's card shows **Cancelled** with the cancellation's own moment, in the usual `02/12/2026, 11:30 PM` form, in the row where **Expiry** used to be. A plan that simply ran out keeps **Expiry**.
- The plan name reads **Firm Plus [Limited Access]**, with the bracketed part in red at 80% of the name's size — also in the side menu's plan row, which shares the same label. The card's big heading keeps the name alone so the tag isn't printed twice on one card.
- The block below is now **Limited Access Mode**, with the sentence chosen by the reason: *"You recently cancelled your subscription plan…"* or *"Your subscription plan has expired…"*, each naming the tier's allowance.
- All four card values — Role, Firm, Current Plan, Expiry/Cancelled — are 14 pt, the block's own body size; the plan stays bold. The 20 pt plan name at the top of the card is unchanged, because it is the card's title rather than one of its values, as the plan said.
- The same wording change reached the list banners (*"Your access is limited…"*), the read-only notices, the paywall's lapsed card and the cancellation warning, in English and Bengali, and the seven case-list mockups carry the new banner sentence.

**Two things worth knowing**
- The card decides "cancelled" by comparing the newest approved purchase of the current tier with the newest cancellation of that tier. A later renewal hides an old cancellation again, so a plan that ran its course is never mislabelled.
- A chamber member has no cancellation record of their own, so a member of a cancelled chamber reads the "expired" sentence. Their card still says Limited Access; only the reason sentence differs.

Which means for a purchase on Jan 31, the plan ends Feb 28 (28 days), not 31. Also for a purchase on Oct 21 + 1 month = Nov 21 — that's 31 days later (Oct 21 → Nov 21 is 31 days). Actually the user's concern was "buy at 21st October, plan doesn't end abruptly at 31st October" — with calendar-month arithmetic it ends Nov 21, so fine. 5. **Naming:** DB columns `snake_case`, Dart/JSON `camelCase`, Drift auto-mapping between them.
6. **Comments:** short intent comments on every file and major section. Never delete existing comments unless they conflict with new logic.
7. **No `BackdropFilter` anywhere** — use the performance-safe alternatives from the plan.
8. **Mobile-first only.** No tablet/desktop optimization yet.
9. **Mockups follow the app, not the other way round:** every mockup screen has been built and the app is nearly complete, so a screen's shipped body is the source of truth and may depart from its mockup where the app has changed. 10. **Rev 2.4 scope contract:** editable court categories/courts/steps/case types/on-behalfs are domain-synced and firm-shared in firm mode; language, view, navigation, notification, and backup-nudge settings are always per-user.
11. **Casing:** in user-facing English, **titles, headings and labels** are written in **standard title case** — capitalise the first and last word and every major word (noun, pronoun, verb, adjective, adverb, subordinating conjunction), and keep the **minor words lower-case** unless they are first or last: articles (*a*, *an*, *the*), coordinating conjunctions (*and*, *or*, *but*, *nor*, *so*, *yet*) and short prepositions (*of*, *to*, *in*, *on*, *at*, *by*, *for*, *with*, *from*) — so it is **What the App Offers**, never *What The App Offers*. **Text that reads as a general sentence — an info line, helper text, description, dialog or body sentence — is sentence case**, however it is styled, and **prose bodies and paragraphs** use sentence case too: only the first word and proper nouns are capitalised. as $$
declare
  v_user uuid := auth.uid();

begin

-- The roll-out window is simulated through `app.device_rollout_end`, the seam
-- the migrations expose for exactly this: the checks that must refuse a device
-- run against a date after the window, and the grand-fathering check runs
-- against the live default.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

returns void

begin

{"kind":"tool","id":"XfKQtxGYArI","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"supabase/migrations/20261022120000_device_trim_counts_the_caller.sql","instructions":"Re-issue device_trim_surplus so a caller holding no slot is not counted as occupying one","content":"-- Device trim counts the caller only when it holds a slot.
--
-- The proof `supabase/tests/device_limit_test.sql` caught this on its first run:
-- a third sign-in on a two-device Pro account was **admitted**, and one of the
-- two devices already holding the slots was revoked as `lapse` — the plan-full
-- screen could never appear, and the lawyer's other phone was told the plan had
-- changed when nothing had.
--
-- The cause was here. `register_device` trims before it knows whether the caller
-- already has a row, and this function always kept `p_cap - 1` devices *other
-- than the caller* — arithmetic that is right only when the caller occupies one
-- of the slots. A brand-new device holds none, so the first trim of its
-- registration threw away a legitimate device and then found a free slot.
--
-- The fix is to ask the table instead of assuming: a caller with an active row
-- keeps the cap minus its own slot, and a caller with no row leaves the whole
-- cap to the devices that are actually there. Trimming above the cap still
-- happens for both — a fallen ceiling, or an account that is over it, is
-- trimmed to the cap and no further, so a new device still meets the plan-full
-- rules rather than a silent eviction.
--
-- Everything else is unchanged: the function returns without touching anything
-- while the account has no live plan, revokes the surplus as `lapse` (not
-- `cap`, so the owner is told the plan changed), clears the evicted devices'
-- push tokens in the same statement pair, and never revokes the caller.

create or replace function public.device_trim_surplus(
  p_user_id uuid,
  p_session_id uuid,
  p_cap integer
)
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
declare
  v_holds_slot boolean;
  v_ids uuid[];
  v_keys text[];
begin
  if not public.has_sync_entitlement(p_user_id) then
    return;
  end if;

  -- Does the caller already hold one of the slots? A brand-new device does not,
  -- and must not be counted as if it did.
  v_holds_slot := exists (
    select 1
      from public.user_devices d
     where d.user_id = p_user_id
       and d.session_id = p_session_id
       and d.revoked_at is null
  );

  select array_agg(s.id), array_agg(s.device_key)
    into v_ids, v_keys
    from (
      select d.id, d.device_key
        from public.user_devices d
       where d.user_id = p_user_id
         and d.revoked_at is null
         and d.session_id is distinct from p_session_id
       order by d.last_seen_at desc
       offset greatest(p_cap - case when v_holds_slot then 1 else 0 end, 0)
    ) s;

  if v_ids is null then
    return;
  end if;

  update public.user_devices d
     set revoked_at = now(),
         revoked_reason = 'lapse'
   where d.id = any(v_ids);

  delete from public.device_tokens t
   where t.user_id = p_user_id
     and t.device_key = any(v_keys);
end;
$$;

The caller counts against the cap only when it already holds an active row, so a device signing in for the first time does not evict a device that does.';
"}}

-- "The tier in force right now", which is `tier` until the instant a waiting
-- downgrade starts and `tier_pending` from that instant on. Every reader takes
-- this rather than the raw column, so no gate re-implements the waiting rule.
--
-- `stable`, not `immutable`, and the label is load-bearing: the body reads
-- `now()`, so the same arguments do **not** always give the same answer. Marking
-- it immutable would let the planner fold one call at plan time and reuse that
-- answer for the rest of the statement — the exact mid-term flip this function
-- exists to express, frozen.
create or replace function public.effective_tier(p_tier text, p_pending text, p_from timestamptz)
returns text
language sql
stable
as $$
  select case
    when p_pending is null then coalesce(p_tier, 'free')
    when p_from is not null and now() >= p_from then p_pending
    else coalesce(p_tier, 'free')
  end;
$$;

The device limit is now live on the real database, and the proof you asked for prints `DEVICE OK`. It failed its first run — and that failure was worth having, because it found a genuine bug that would have hit lawyers.

**What happened when I ran it**

The first run was refused at the very first check: a third sign-in on a two-device Pro account was **let in**, and one of the two phones already holding a slot was quietly signed out with the message *your plan changed*. The cause was arithmetic in the "trim the surplus" step: it kept one fewer device than the cap by assuming the newcomer already occupied a slot, and the newcomer doesn't. The fix asks the device table whether the caller actually holds a slot before subtracting one, in a new migration [20261022120000_device_trim_counts_the_caller.sql](supabase/migrations/20261022120000_device_trim_counts_the_caller.sql). A full plan now answers "plan full" as it should, and an account genuinely over its cap is still trimmed back to it.

Three further failures were the proof's own mistakes, not the server's, so I repaired the proof rather than bending the server to match it: it filled only one of a lapsed Pro's two slots and then expected a refusal; it tried to read the private device table as a signed-in client; and its roll-out-window pair used one window plus a date inside it, which can never both be true.

**Where things stand**

- The live project `lsthasywrdrhuuxnykau` records **60 migrations**, has the `user_devices` table, and all ten device functions are in place — I read that back from the database, not from my notes.
- `supabase/tests/device_limit_test.sql` prints `DEVICE OK` with a clean exit.
- `flutter analyze` is clean and the full suite is **1934 passed**; the two guards that count migrations now expect 60 and the newest file, and the SQL ledger was regenerated and passes its `--check`.
- Version **0.0.566** is recorded, with the plan bullet, Task 22's Phase 6 section and [currentlyWorking.md](docs/currentlyWorking.md) updated to say applied-and-proved, including the defect found.

**What still needs a human**

+++ supabase\migrations\20261022120000_device_trim_counts_the_caller.sql	after
@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+-- Device trim counts the caller only when it holds a slot.
+--
+-- The proof `supabase/tests/device_limit_test.sql` caught this on its first run:
+-- a third sign-in on a two-device Pro account was **admitted**, and one of the
+-- two devices already holding the slots was revoked as `lapse` — the plan-full
+-- screen could never appear, and the lawyer's other phone was told the plan had
+-- changed when nothing had.
+--
+-- The cause was here. `register_device` trims before it knows whether the caller
+-- already has a row, and this function always kept `p_cap - 1` devices *other
+-- than the caller* — arithmetic that is right only when the caller occupies one
+-- of the slots. A brand-new device holds none, so the first trim of its
+-- registration threw away a legitimate device and then found a free slot.
+--
+-- The fix is to ask the table instead of assuming: a caller with an active row
+-- keeps the cap minus its own slot, and a caller with no row leaves the whole
+-- cap to the devices that are actually there. Trimming above the cap still
+-- happens for both — a fallen ceiling, or an account that is over it, is
+-- trimmed to the cap and no further, so a new device still meets the plan-full
+-- rules rather than a silent eviction.
+--
+-- Everything else is unchanged: the function returns without touching anything
+-- while the account has no live plan, revokes the surplus as `lapse` (not
+-- `cap`, so the owner is told the plan changed), clears the evicted devices'
+-- push tokens in the same statement pair, and never revokes the caller.
+
+create or replace function public.device_trim_surplus(
+  p_user_id uuid,
+  p_session_id uuid,
+  p_cap integer
+)
+returns void
+language plpgsql
+security definer
+set search_path = pg_catalog, public
+as $$
+declare
+  v_holds_slot boolean;
+  v_ids uuid[];
+  v_keys text[];
+begin
+  if not public.has_sync_entitlement(p_user_id) then
+    return;
+  end if;
+
+  -- Does the caller already hold one of the slots? A brand-new device does not,
+  -- and must not be counted as if it did.
+  v_holds_slot := exists (
+    select 1
+      from public.user_devices d
+     where d.user_id = p_user_id
+       and d.session_id = p_session_id
+       and d.revoked_at is null
+  );
+
+  select array_agg(s.id), array_agg(s.device_key)
+    into v_ids, v_keys
+    from (
+      select d.id, d.device_key
+        from public.user_devices d
+       where d.user_id = p_user_id
+         and d.revoked_at is null
+         and d.session_id is distinct from p_session_id
+       order by d.last_seen_at desc
+       offset greatest(p_cap - case when v_holds_slot then 1 else 0 end, 0)
+    ) s;
+
+  if v_ids is null then
+    return;
+  end if;
+
+  update public.user_devices d
+     set revoked_at = now(),
+         revoked_reason = 'lapse'
+   where d.id = any(v_ids);
+
+  delete from public.device_tokens t
+   where t.user_id = p_user_id
+     and t.device_key = any(v_keys);
+end;
+$$;
+
+comment on function public.device_trim_surplus(uuid, uuid, integer) is
+  'Revokes the devices above the cap after the ceiling falls (downgrade, lapse and renewal), least recently seen first and never the caller, and only while the account has a live plan. The caller counts against the cap only when it already holds an active row, so a device signing in for the first time does not evict a device that does.';

- No automated test proves the order the user cares about — **save, then acknowledge, then erase**. The revoked-screen test only pins the failure branch, so a future edit could wipe a device whose work never left it and every test would still pass.

{"kind":"tool","id":"Xzg2otbJmKw","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"supabase/migrations/20261022130000_device_push_rollout_window.sql","instructions":"Re-issue device_may_push so an unregistered session may still push until the same roll-out date reads use.","content":"-- ===========================================================================
-- Device limit (3/3) — writes get the same roll-out window as reads.
--
-- **Why.** `20261022110000` gave an unregistered session ("an install that has
-- not updated yet") until `device_rollout_end()` to READ, so the update strands
-- nobody, but gave it no such allowance to WRITE. The result was the opposite
-- of the promise in the plan: an install that had not updated could pull the
-- account's diary down and could not hand a single edit back up. Its queued
-- mutations were refused as `device_revoked` on the first push, and because a
-- refusal is not retryable the client marked each one `blocked` — visible in
-- Sync Status as *the server refused this change*, but never sent again on its
-- own. A limit that turns a lawyer's backup off silently is worse than one that
-- arrives a month later.
--
-- **What changes.** One branch, the same shape and the same date as
-- `device_may_read`'s: a session with **no row in `user_devices` at all** is
-- admitted to push while `now() < device_rollout_end()`. A session that has a
-- row is not affected in the slightest — an active device is admitted as
-- before, and a revoked device keeps exactly its 14-day flush window.
--
-- **Why this cannot become a loophole.** Revocation in this registry is a
-- timestamp on a row, never a deletion: `revoke_device` and
-- `device_trim_surplus` both `update` `revoked_at`, so every session the server
-- has ever seen a registration for still has its row. The unregistered branch is
-- therefore reachable only by a session that has never called `register_device`
-- — the old install, and nobody else. A device the server revoked, by any
-- reason and at any time, stays refused, including during the window.
--
-- **After the window nothing changes for a revoked device**, and an old install
-- stops writing at the same instant it stops reading: one date closes both
-- gates, so the two halves cannot drift apart again.
-- ===========================================================================

create or replace function public.device_may_push(p_at timestamptz default now())
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = pg_catalog, public
as $$
  select public.current_session_id() is null
      or public.device_is_active()
      -- The roll-out case, identical to device_may_read's: a session that never
      -- registered is an install that has not updated yet, admitted only until
      -- the same date registrations stop being grandfathered.
      or (
           p_at < public.device_rollout_end()
           and not exists (
             select 1
               from public.user_devices d
              where d.user_id = auth.uid()
                and d.session_id = public.current_session_id()
           )
         )
      -- A revoked device may still hand its unsent work over before it erases.
      or exists (
           select 1
             from public.user_devices d
            where d.user_id = auth.uid()
              and d.session_id = public.current_session_id()
              and d.revoked_at is not null
              and d.revoked_at + interval '14 days' > p_at
         );
$$;

A revoked session is never admitted by the roll-out branch, because revocation stamps a row rather than deleting it.';

@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+-- ===========================================================================
+-- Device limit (3/3) — writes get the same roll-out window as reads.
+--
+-- **Why.** `20261022110000` gave an unregistered session ("an install that has
+-- not updated yet") until `device_rollout_end()` to READ, so the update strands
+-- nobody, but gave it no such allowance to WRITE. The result was the opposite
+-- of the promise in the plan: an install that had not updated could pull the
+-- account's diary down and could not hand a single edit back up. Its queued
+-- mutations were refused as `device_revoked` on the first push, and because a
+-- refusal is not retryable the client marked each one `blocked` — visible in
+-- Sync Status as *the server refused this change*, but never sent again on its
+-- own. A limit that turns a lawyer's backup off silently is worse than one that
+-- arrives a month later.
+--
+-- **What changes.** One branch, the same shape and the same date as
+-- `device_may_read`'s: a session with **no row in `user_devices` at all** is
+-- admitted to push while `now() < device_rollout_end()`. A session that has a
+-- row is not affected in the slightest — an active device is admitted as
+-- before, and a revoked device keeps exactly its 14-day flush window.
+--
+-- **Why this cannot become a loophole.** Revocation in this registry is a
+-- timestamp on a row, never a deletion: `revoke_device` and
+-- `device_trim_surplus` both `update` `revoked_at`, so every session the server
+-- has ever seen a registration for still has its row. The unregistered branch is
+-- therefore reachable only by a session that has never called `register_device`
+-- — the old install, and nobody else. A device the server revoked, by any
+-- reason and at any time, stays refused, including during the window.
+--
+-- **After the window nothing changes for a revoked device**, and an old install
+-- stops writing at the same instant it stops reading: one date closes both
+-- gates, so the two halves cannot drift apart again.
+-- ===========================================================================
+
+create or replace function public.device_may_push(p_at timestamptz default now())
+returns boolean
+language sql
+stable
+security definer
+set search_path = pg_catalog, public
+as $$
+  select public.current_session_id() is null
+      or public.device_is_active()
+      -- The roll-out case, identical to device_may_read's: a session that never
+      -- registered is an install that has not updated yet, admitted only until
+      -- the same date registrations stop being grandfathered.
+      or (
+           p_at < public.device_rollout_end()
+           and not exists (
+             select 1
+               from public.user_devices d
+              where d.user_id = auth.uid()
+                and d.session_id = public.current_session_id()
+           )
+         )
+      -- A revoked device may still hand its unsent work over before it erases.
+      or exists (
+           select 1
+             from public.user_devices d
+            where d.user_id = auth.uid()
+              and d.session_id = public.current_session_id()
+              and d.revoked_at is not null
+              and d.revoked_at + interval '14 days' > p_at
+         );
+$$;
+
+comment on function public.device_may_push(timestamptz) is
+  'True for an active device, a revoked device still inside its 14-day flush window, an unregistered session before the roll-out end (2026-11-21), or a caller with no session claim. A revoked session is never admitted by the roll-out branch, because revocation stamps a row rather than deleting it.';

The Daily Cause List's month/year selector now makes a sound when it moves.

**What was wrong:** that selector was asking the phone to play its own "touch" click, and Android only plays that when the phone's touch-sound setting is switched on. That is why it was silent. The Notification Time window doesn't rely on the phone's setting — it plays a short sound bundled inside the app. The calendar now plays that same bundled sound, from the same file, so the two pickers sound identical.

**When it sounds now:** once for each month or year the columns actually move to while you scroll them. It stays silent when the selector opens or closes, when you tap the row already in the middle (nothing moved), on the header's ‹ › arrows, and when you swipe the day grid. The selector also had its old phone click left on for that screen, which would have clicked and ticked at once — that is switched off here only, so every other date picker in the app keeps its click exactly as it was.

**Changed:** [calendar_picker_dialog.dart](legal_case_diary_flutter/lib/shared/widgets/calendar_picker_dialog.dart) (the Daily Cause List calendar — the sound itself), [month_year_picker.dart](legal_case_diary_flutter/lib/shared/widgets/month_year_picker.dart) (one on/off switch so this screen can replace the click, default unchanged for everyone else), plus the plan, Task 09 and [currentlyWorking.md](legal_case_diary_flutter/docs/currentlyWorking.md).

**Verified:** `flutter analyze` clean, full `flutter test` **1973 passed**, version **0.0.607** recorded. The new test proves the selector is silent when it opens, ticks once for one year move, once for one month move, does not tick again when the held row is confirmed, and that no phone click joins the tick. What a test cannot prove is how it sounds on your phone — that needs one scroll on a real device.

No database, server or mockup changes; a sound is not a screen body.

### 2026-10-26 — A chamber buyer keeps the seats before the firm exists — COMPLETE (0.0.645)

- **What was reported.** A free user bought **Firm — 1 Month**; after approval Manage Plan still showed **Devices 1 of 1**. The account had `tier = firm` but `firm_id = null`, so it fell to the one-per-member device cap.
- **The ruling applied.** The owner pays for the seats, so a chamber-tier account with **no chamber** (an owner-designate) may use the tier's full slots for its own devices until an associate joins. Firm 5 / Firm Plus 10 / Enterprise 20.
- **Server.** `20261026130000_owner_designate_device_slots.sql` re-issues `device_cap`: a chamber owner still reads `slots − associates`, a seated associate 1, a capacity-signed-out associate 0, a chamber-tier account with no chamber its **full tier seat cap**, and non-chamber tiers their own caps. **Applied live** — the project now records **72 versions**; `supabase/tests/firm_capacity_test.sql` prints **CAPACITY OK** with the new owner-designate cases (including Pro 2 / Starter 1 / Free 1 unchanged).
- **Client.** The post-payment approval watch now **re-registers this device** when the subscription changes, so the device gate's cap (and Manage Plan's devices meter) picks up the new number without a relaunch. A cold start registers anyway. `device_cap_parity_test.dart` pins the new branch; the watch test asserts the gate refresh happens exactly once when the expiry changes.
- **Checks.** `flutter analyze` clean; full `flutter test` **2,100 passed**; ledger regenerated to **72 migrations** and `--check` clean; the live account that reported the issue now reads `device_cap = 5`.
- **Docs.** Plan, Task 22, the manual checklist (new **Scenario 16** and §12.11 SQL check), `supabase/README.md`, and the capacity/device memories updated.
- **Remaining.** The physical check in Scenario 16 is outstanding. If the owner fills all five slots with their own devices, adding the first associate needs one device signed out first — the card's “5 devices **or** 4 associates”.

### 2026-10-26 — Renewals stop the post-payment watch too — COMPLETE (0.0.644)

- **What was asked.** Follow-up to 0.0.643: an **already-premium** renewal or plan change kept the 30-second polling until the ten-minute window even after the plan appeared, because the early stop only recognised free → premium.
- **What changed.** The watch now captures the account's **governing expiry** when it starts — the profile's for an individual, the firm's for a chamber account, through the same `resolveSubscriptionExpiry` the entitlement uses — and re-reads it after every **successful** refresh. Any change ends the watch on that beat, so renewals, upgrades and queued downgrades stop as quickly as a free → premium approval. The free → premium check remains only as the fallback when the start expiry could not be read; a failed refresh compares nothing. A rejection moves no expiry, so it still runs to the window. No server change.
- **Checks.** `flutter analyze` clean; full `flutter test` **2,100 passed**; the new case starts with the account already premium and moves the expiry on the first beat — one refresh, then the watch is stopped and later beats do nothing (the old behaviour would have kept polling).
- **Remaining.** A rejected payment still polls to the ten-minute limit; stopping on the ledger's resolution (one extra read per tick) was considered and not added.

### 2026-10-26 — An approval applies itself without a sign-out — COMPLETE (0.0.643)

- **What was reported.** After a free user bought a plan and an admin approved it, the app kept showing **Free** for minutes; only signing out and back in applied the plan.
- **Why.** A free account deliberately holds no Realtime socket (sync is entitlement-gated) and there is no approval push, so nothing told the app. Its profile cache is re-read only on launch, resume, reconnect or sign-in — none of which happens while the payer waits in the app.
- **What changed.** The checkout now starts a bounded watch after a confirmed submission (`payment_approval_watch.dart`): every **30 seconds for 10 minutes** it re-reads the account — pulling the profile and firm and recomputing premium — and invalidates both Subscription History ledgers on the same beat, so the plan, gates and pending row update while the payer waits. It stops early when a free account turns premium, pauses while the app is backgrounded (the resume refresh covers that), and a second submission restarts the window. No server change; no new copy.
- **Checks.** `flutter analyze` clean; full `flutter test` **2,099 passed**; new tests cover the 30-second beat, the end of the window, a restart, and the checkout starting the watch.
